cross_checks: back wall floor edge 3944 == floor's long side
right wall floor edge 3031 == floor's short side 3030
opposite walls differ by the notch: back 3944 - front 3486 = 458; right 3030 - left 2960 = 70
orientation: The faces are a cubemap from ONE camera, so their order is fixed by yaw:
front 0deg, right 90, back 180, left 270. Walking front -> right -> back -> left
is therefore a real rotational direction, not a guess, and the floor polygon
is now traversed in exactly that order. The first version ran the other way,
which mirrored the room and put both doors on the wrong side.
Facing any wall, the RIGHT of that photo is the next face clockwise in yaw:
in the back photo the balcony sits at the right, and 180+90 = 270 = left face,
so the left face IS the balcony wall. The front photo agrees: balcony at its
left, and 0-90 = 270. Two independent faces, same answer.

walls.note: 2960 — BALCONY wall, sliding door not measured

openings.note: 1549 measured from the photo's left edge; facing the right wall, the photo's left is the FRONT corner, which is where this edge starts

890 x 2051 measured. In the back photo the door sits hard against the corner OPPOSITE the balcony; facing back, the photo's left is the RIGHT-wall corner, which is where this edge starts. 60 mm return is estimated, the end it sits at is not

features.note: the back photo puts its notch at the balcony end and the front photo puts its notch at the balcony end too, so the beam runs along the balcony wall. The right face also shows a notch, which this does not explain — see caveats

caveats: The BALCONY OPENING IS MISSING — the left face was never annotated, so the sliding door has no width, height or sill anywhere.

The right face shows a ceiling notch its position cannot explain if the beam runs along the balcony wall. Either there is a second beam over the bathroom door, or one of the three notch readings belongs to something else.
The main door's 60 mm return from the corner is estimated; which corner it sits against is not.
The front wall's floor edge was marked '?' and is taken from the floor face.
